physical_hypothesis_update.conditional_variable_region_light_crossi: R <= 0.033/(1+z) for coherent flux change within about 40 observed days

scientific_inference_rules: Use all four interleaved October 2023 F150W epochs before claiming a constant 2023 emission line; four independent-date nondetections constrain persistence.
Do not compare total predicted 5.5 nJy with an uncorrected 0.12 arcsecond aperture without a PSF-recovery fraction.
Treat illustrative 6.3-7.9 sigma discrepancy as conditional diagnostic, NOT as finalized injected-source-calibrated significance.
A source non-detection in a 2022 image alone can be explained by onset before August 2023, whereas nondetections within October 2023 between August and November are a stronger constraint.
A photometric non-detection in October cannot by itself prove the nature, wavelength identity, or physical distance of the August/November emission line.
Positive recovery of three neighboring galaxies and no source in a 0.15 arcsecond coordinate grid disfavor trivial local sky-registration errors but do not prove perfect MOCSS astrometry.
No JADES DR4 NIRSpec target within 5 arcseconds means no spectroscopic redshift is established for the orphan or its three near-one-arcsecond neighbors by that catalogue.
Coherent month-scale variability conditionally limits the variable region's light-crossing size, not any surrounding static gas or alleged gas-trail length.
No known directed gas trail follows from source RA/Dec or from spectrograph dispersion; never invent its axis, terminal point, or distance.
The [OIII] 4960A line expected from the 16004A/5008A identification is near 15850.79A, not 15864A; re-extraction remains a priority.

An error-propagated scenario calculation must carry the 12-percent NIRSpec line-flux uncertainty and explicitly stress correlated October F150W noise; 6.3–7.9 sigma from the earlier illustrative diagnostic is NOT a defensible calibrated exclusion or a universal sensitivity bound.
The effective aperture factor includes source PSF, local annulus subtraction and blending, not merely an encircled-energy curve; empirical injection/recovery remains absent.
Do not infer PROVEN_VARIABLE or rule out constant emission before common-blank-sky covariance, PSF+annulus injection and stage-2 NIRSpec flux and astrometry have been measured.

The October 2023 cross-image covariance is now estimated from 95 matched sky apertures in four original JWST F150W SCI mosaics and their pinned SHA-256. Its fixed-weight sigma ~0.663 nJy is larger than ~0.521 nJy diagonal-only, but common astrophysical sky structure is not instrument noise.

latest_sensitivity_followup.interpretation: Previous 6.3–7.9 sigma estimate excluded the published spectral flux statistical uncertainty and assumed independent mosaics; updated conditional scenarios are materially less decisive. No final p-value or detection-exclusion significance has been measured.

latest_measured_covariance_followup.remaining_test: Calibrated NIRCam PSF injection with actual mosaic-specific drizzle PSF; reprocess NIRSpec line/controls 16004, 15850.793,13656.748 Angstrom with Stage 2 and measured point-source throughput.
